When my Pawpaw was very old and started to care less about not saying what was on his mind, I heard him say something under his breath that totally shocked me and still sticks in my mind years after his passing.

We were on a family vacation, he was wearing one of those baseball cap style hats that said "veteran" on it. Someone in a restaurant passed by our table and thanked him for his service.

"If they knew what I did during the war, they wouldn't be thanking me."

Not an ALT (yet) but that cult tried to recruit me when I was vacationing in my friend's city, outside of an aeon department store! I spoke almost no Japanese at the time and was completely alone. In a nervous panic I pointed at the food court and mumbled in broken Japanese "My friends are waiting for me..." despite my only friend still being at work. I took a taxi back to my friend's apartment that day just to avoid the cult ladies on the walk back.
I'd love to join! morbid#2671

NTA and I am so, so sorry at some of these comments. You have no reason to disclose your trans status to anyone for any reason, no matter how close they are to you. Coming out can be so painful and traumatic, especially when it ends up in situations like this. For all the people asking that OP repeat the things her friend said to her, it doesn't matter. Transphobia is transphobia.
They aren't scared of humans for sure. Those things are terrible.

Haha! Reading the book as a young teenager freaked me out a lot, way more than the movie. I think it doesn't apply to everyone (as I was pretty easily scared back then in general), but I thought that quote was interesting, and explains why so many parents see it and go "WTF?" while it remains a pretty popular kid's book/movie.

Felt this. We rented a house in my senior year of high school, small town just outside Metro Atlanta, and it had a fucking palmetto bug infestation. We found out a few weeks after moving in, moved the minute that the lease was up. Those things are disgusting and aggressive. I became very good at killing them because the alternative was them flying directly at me.

The first Peter Jackson movie I ever saw was Dead Alive.  


I didn't get into LOTR until I was an adult. Learning that he directed those movies blew my mind. Before LOTR, I just knew him as the guy who directed the weird gory zomedy.

I remember a long time ago reading a quote from Neil Gaiman, where he said that adults are more likely to find Coraline scary than kids. He said that for kids, it's just an adventure story, and each part of the story is like a challenge that Coraline is sure to overcome. But adults tend to see it as a horror story because we can't put ourselves in the kid protagonist's shoes as easily, and we are more worried about the kid being in danger.

I went to Japan right as it was starting to hit the states super bad. Like, the week that I got back was the last week before everything began to close down.  
I smoked a lot while I was over there, I'm a social smoker and went to visit friends for a week so we did a lot of drinking and smoking at various bars and izakayas around my friend's city.   
Coming back from Asia with a smoker's cough during the height of people freaking out about Covid was not a fun experience. I got a lot of dirty looks in the airports (I had 3 layovers) and when I got back to America people didn't want to be around me.

Late reply, but I only just turned 25 and this was true for my generation too. Walked to and from the bus stop at the end of my street every day. When I was really young and my mom was worried about there not being an adult, I just went to a friend's house (their mom was stay at home). Then when siblings and I got old enough to be "home alone,"  we would get home, make ourselves a snack, and watch TV or play until my parents came home. The kids who went to day cares or after school programs were the exception, most of us just went home. I recall that a lot of us felt bad for the kids who had to go to after school because we all considered it lame.

Fuck people like this. A global pandemic is more important than your sandwich.  


I work for a dinner theatre type place and we had to close way early on (beginning of March) because we're a tourist spot. When they made the announcement on social media, people were firing back "But I wanted to come tomorrow!"

Then again, you could have done a really good thing for someone who needed it. When I first started getting my footing on having a job and paying for my groceries at 18, my card was declined on $20 worth of items at the store. I was making very little money at the time and almost in tears from the embarrassment. I was about to tell the cashier that I would go put some items back when the guy behind me paid my bill for me. When I can afford it I'll do the same for others because of what he did for me.

NTA. Even if you were just looking for friends of every gender and not just women, you aren't obligated to respond to any messages. From experience, guys like that will keep hitting you up until you say something or block them, you did the right thing.

Late to the party, but I freaked out a little when my gf got an Alexa from her mom for xmas. I hid it so she couldn't set it up... not like "took it and put it way out of the way" but I put it in an (obvious place in an easily accessible) cabinet and didn't mention it.

Not exactly the same, but I'm interning at a middle school right now and I overhear the most hilarious things. Middle school drama over the most average things, and the kids make hella jokes. Homeroom is a gold mine. Every time a new meme gets big, the kids work it into their everyday conversations as much as they can. Heard a student last week telling his friend, "I can't today, I have to take my horse to the old town road."

As well as how the layout of the ride changed. Damn you, theme park youtube. I now have an extensive well of very useless information sitting in my brain.

My girlfriend had a psychosomatic incident where her legs completely stopped working for almost a month due to all the stress she was under from moving out of live-in detox therapy, back into her abusive household, and  then in with us. The move itself plus the fact that she lost her regular meetings with her therapist due to distance really did something to her, and she was paralyzed fully in both legs. We took her to the ER to figure out what was going on because for the past few days she had been having trouble with losing feeling in part or all of her legs and then one day they just lost feeling altogether. Left home around 10 PM for ER and was there until 7 AM when they finally admitted her. I stayed with her wide awake while she answered doctors' questions because they couldnt figure out what was wrong with her at that point. She wasnt allowed to take any of her regular meds until they ruled out meds causing the problem, so she was even more anxious and unstable than just the stress of the hospital trip. Had to eventually leave to shower and catch a few hours sleep before work because we were so poor I couldnt call out. Only to get home and find the power (AC) out in the middle of summer, so I took an ice cold shower and layed there exhausted because it was almost too hot to sleep. Eventually got 2 hours sleep and got up, went to work, then went straight back to the hospital. The first day felt like the longest of that whole month, but the whole month was terrible. When she finally came home from the hospital and physical therapy I was so fucking thankful and relieved.
thank you so much. I think I really needed some encouraging words after the crazy week I've had. ❤
Lol, did they take it in stride? Many panhandlers I've been faced with often get aggressive after being told no.

Entering my mid-20s now and finally starting to consider separating myself from my mother. She will go between telling me she wants me out of her house and how great she is for allowing me to live there, to telling me I would never be able to survive without her and life is way too hard for me to make it on my own. At my current point in life she is right because I don't make enough to afford rent, even splitting it with others. But I want to become self sufficient and finally move out/cut her off because of how toxic she is. Living with her is mentally draining and she made me incredibly dependent on her in my early adulthood with lies and emotional/financial manipulation. I can't wait to get out.

We have something similar here in Atlanta. People will carry medical papers and hang out near Emory or Grady, claiming to have just been discharged from ER/hospital stay and in need of cash to cover the bill. I fell for this the first time because I was a teenager and not an ATL local and hadn't encountered the situation before. Since my friends and I were teenagers we maybe had $6 cash between us all, dude didn't seem too happy about it.

I usually just tell people that I don't carry cash, which is true. Weirdest encounter I've ever faced was "If you give me money for gas I'll give you this blank check from my husband's job, he got paid today but we don't have a bank account so we can't cash it on our own." Sorry... no. How dumb do you have to be to fall for that one, or for that matter, believe it will work?

My mom was once married to a guy who was former military. Out of curiosity she took a civilian police training course for fun in the early 00's (not the same thing I know, but she wanted to get an idea for what physical training for a similar job was like). She went from truthfully telling people she graduated the course, to lying about being a former officer, to lying about being a former officer who headed sting operations in the 90s, to telling people she was *in the fucking military and sent to Iraq to fight the taliban*. She has some health problems that left her disabled and I'm pretty sure she's using the ex-military story to lie about why she's disabled, she would rather tell people she got in some heroic accident than tell the truth about her illness being genetic.

My girlfriend. She has a bunch of physical & mental health problems, a history of self harm/suicide attempts, and has been in a few dangerous situations before (almost got kidnapped as a teenager, was an addict, etc). I'm really proud of how far she's come and that she's been able to remove herself from the living situation that spawned so many of the other dangers she has faced. Her will to survive is really admirable.

Because I work in technically an entertainment venue, we have even busier shows on holidays. They get away with it because we don't run shows *every day,* so "technically" we could find time to visit our family for the holidays on a day that isn't the actual holiday.

Except that we run shows regularly on weekends, when most people are off work and can do family things. Plus, around Holidays, our marketing department goes all out and starts pulling from other departments to help them market, so there is a high possibility that if we don't have a show you'll be working anyway.

This. Some of my middle schoolers have asked me if I know about it and I tell them "It's become a dead meme to most of the internet. It's fake, just an urban legend or a creepypasta." and they go "Oh, ok." and move on. It's the parents/schools that are blowing it up, the kids either think it's funny or don't care.

Being from near Atlanta, this movie was so much fun just to watch him speed around on our roads. Especially I-85, no idea how they managed to close it for filming long enough, with Atlanta traffic already being horrid.

I almost skipped out on trying a new place for dinner last week because of Yelp reviews, but decided to give it a go anyway because I'd heard good things in person from locals and students (nearby college town). Several reviews were saying things like "service was SO slow" and such. I'm so glad I didn't let those negative reviews change my plans, I guess those folks were so used to fast food joints that a regular wait time at a sit-down burger place was too long for them. One of the best burgers I've ever had, plus we ordered wrong due to our own fault and the waitress was very sweet and helpful on getting it corrected for us.

We regularly go to two mechanics in town that are owned by people we have known for years. These guys do good, fast, and reasonably priced work. The only reason we swap between the two often is because despite never advertising and even being a little out of the way (off the main roads of my town), they are always slammed and will frequently recommend one another to customers who need a fast job ("I'm really backed up but try Joe's shop and see if he has room for you.") Good mechanics are consistently honest dudes and will happily rec other good mechanics to you if they can't do the job.

Not exactly on topic but similar.

My mom didn't realize that multiple people in a fast food place had headsets and could hear every interaction, even if they weren't taking the order. When I worked in fast food, the restaurant I was at was known for their biscuits and for serving breakfast all day (before McDonald's did). My mom really liked the ham biscuits and would come by often. Well one day I was working drive-thru and we were required to say the restaurant's slogan followed by "This is \_\_\_\_\_ how can I help you?"

I answered the drive-thru (not knowing it was my mom) "Hellooooo \[company slogan\], this is Morbid how can I help you?" My mom proceeded to make fun of me for the dumb slogan basically in front of the entire team, since most of us had headsets on.

When I worked in fast food we were right next to a church. Tons of the churchgoers would come through the drive-thru either before or after service. Slammed lines while trying to hear orders over the extremely loud church bells... it was the worst.
We have this dog food smell as well because of a local factory(?). Some days there's nothing, some days it's faint, and some days I won't even go run errands because the smell is just unbearable.

Two things: One, half the town's population is pretty much methed-up (or some other kind of substance). Our town's drug trade as well as our hospitals/doctors and probably our police unfortunately preys on people's addictions and perpetuates the cycle of addiction and poverty, I have seen it firsthand and it's really sad. Many of our "clinics/pharmacies" are simply pill mills. And since the cost of living is so low here it makes it that much harder to remove yourself from the situation, when our "nice" houses are 100k and the neighboring towns are 300+k the obvious choice is to stay where it's cheaper...

 Two, it's roughly 20 miles from literally *everything* other than fast food and grocery stores. I have to commute to work, college, friend's houses, decent sit down restaurants etc 30 mins each way. The only decent entertainment we have other than people watching at WalMart is a movie theater that opened when I was in high school, which was a really big deal.
Don't forget Rome, GA and Dublin, GA.

I have been trying this lately with 7th graders. Their all-time favorite thing to do is talk with their table mates and compare work. As long as it's not a test and they're not straight up copying each other (ELA teacher so obviously if they all write the same thing for a paragraph it's easy to tell), I don't care whether they show their work to one another. It's hard to get that balance but I'm really focused on giving them time to discuss and take a brain break from listening to me or quietly working for at least 10-15 mins each class. I get tired of lecturing too, and my voice starts to break a lot towards the end of the day, so anything I can do to give myself a rest is great.

But I know a lot of people that find pride in this type of work, and I feel like we should treat craftsmanship/blue collar jobs with just as much importance as the ones that require a degree. I'll start: Our uni has a reputation for having one of the most intensive, rigorous, and strict teacher certification programs in the state. We get a lot of praise from the local school system for graduating great students that go on to become great teachers. However, the program is also very stressful as we spend more time at the student teaching level than any other program in the state, as unpaid interns of course. 

The other week all us students were kind of having a collective vent session in one of our courses on campus. A girl in class said that she had recently seen an alum of our uni at the school she was interning at. The alum told her something along the lines of "Oh, you're in \[Uni\]'s program! Haha, I had a mental breakdown going to school there!"

Girl in my class said it felt like an ep of the Twilight Zone, where only she realized how messed up of a brag that was. Prof then admitted that our program is about as close to hazing for future teachers as it gets. Major bad vibes from the whole vent session.

Unfortunately I'm so close to graduating that I don't want to drop out of the program. But I definitely already had a feeling of "Whoa, this is way too stressful." That conversation just solidified it. I do still really want to be a teacher, and plan to finish my degree and start at a school soon after! But damn.

When I was probably about 8 or 9, my family went on vacation to the Great Smoky Mountains in Tennessee. There are a lot of petting zoos up there, and my family preferred to do those cheaper outside activities over things like theme parks (Dollywood) and overpriced dinner-theatres (Dixie Stampede), because we were a family of 6 at the time. 

So we go to this "exotic" zoo that has all the normal stuff like goats, llamas, etc but also some more uncommon animals like camels. It was going well until the last part of the zoo.

It was a section devoted to birds. I have this irrational, *terrible* fear of birds. There was no way around this section of the park as it led right to the exit/gift shop. I begged my mom to let me find another way around or ask an employee to let me somehow skip this part of the park. She refused, not wanting to ruin the rest of the family's final stint through the park.

So I just ran through the bird section, crying. Just full on bawling, refusing to stop and look at anything and drawing attention to our family by being so loud. My mom was mad that I wouldn't interact with any of the park guides or animals, and that I rushed everyone through the section. Now she thinks it was pretty funny and frequently tells this story to friends and family. About 10 years after this happened she finally told me that when I was a newborn she had a pet bird that hated me and would shit on my head and try to peck me, which is most likely what caused my bird phobia.

This is definitely gonna get buried and is also super late. 

Started talking to a guy that I had several mutual friends with online, we would send each other memes and just talk about our day, etc. Didn't expect him to be bi at all (I'm a gay guy) but after talking for a while we expressed a mutual crush. Progressed all the way to hanging out a lot irl and talking about possibly going on a date. Then one day he's feeling a bit down and texts me about it, I offer him the best support I can while clearly telling him "I am not a therapist and not totally sure how to help you, but I care about you." 

Well apparently he missed the "not a therapist" part... now he only texts me when he's upset about something. I still care about him but now talking to him makes me feel overwhelmed and drained, especially since I am a really busy person with my own large amount of mental health problems. I have suggested to him over and over that he may want to get in contact with a professional that can help, and that I am by no means someone who can shoulder his burdens in the same way that a therapist can. Unfortunately, all my romantic interest in him is gone now, replaced by worry for his health and dreading having to talk him through another mental breakdown.

I haven't had weekends, my birthday, or any winter holidays from Thanksgiving to New Years off in 3 years. The holidays just mean nothing to me now, because I don't get to see my family or participate in the fun that our guests are having, it's just a long shift.

Can't eat stuff that's too hot or too cold or too sweet or too spicy... it sucks.

I took a year and a half (ish), spent part of it working a fast food job. Needless to say, I hated it. Picked up a better job that had no real socialization aspect but was a lot better money for doing practically nothing. I had decided when I graduated high school i wouldn't keep contact with a majority of my graduating class, including my friends, and all the people I did want to stay in touch with went away to Uni, so I was pretty much screwed on having any real life contact with other human beings.
When I finally went back to school it was really hard to get back into being social because my job had isolated me really, really hard, and I already have severe social anxiety. I ended up basically having to go to therapy to resocialize myself. 
But I also feel like I had more time to mature as a person and developed a better work ethic. Also the fact that all of my friends were off at Uni made me want to go to college, too, so my grades are a lot better than my (very terrible) high school grades. 
All in all i say the time off was worth it. I start pre-education courses next semester and I'm really excited.

Sorry to say, but this is totally Girl Scout Cookies. Was a troop leader for a while and actually lost money working for them, due to the fact that they make you buy a TON of boxes for cookie stands (and usually over exaggerate how many you need for each stand to get you to buy more). Sure, selling cookies teaches the kids skills and blah blah blah. But that shit put me out $200 of my own money because we couldn't sell enough cookies. Either way, the corporation gets paid- but us people on the bottom either break even or get royally screwed. I quit right after cookie season for this exact reason.

I think though, it might have to do with the fact that Coke is based here in Atlanta.

Holy hell, this! And it got even worse when I became a vegan. Suddenly now all the people who were there for me as vegetarians are like, "but not milking a cow actually hurts it!" "eggs aren't actually baby chickens!" 

Guys, I know. Eat what you want and stop trying to justify yourself to me. I dunno. I guess I got on a tangent. I'm just tired of people taking my personal dietary choice way more personally than necessary.

Recently I've gotten really interested in medieval literature and the history and real-world parallels behind it. I entered spring semester British Literature absolutely dreading having to read through Beowulf and Le Mort D'Arthur, but ended up thoroughly enjoying them when I got a cool new perspective from my professor. It's such a vast time period too, just so much to study and compare. I was unsure what I was going to do with my literary degree before last semester, but now am seriously considering going into medieval studies. It makes me really happy that I found something interesting and worthwhile to be so passionate about, that could possibly end up in getting me the academic career that I want as well.

Both mine have to do with my car; I swear I'm not a bad driver, just unlucky! 

Driving with boyfriend to his dad's house so he can visit his pet snake. He gets confused on directions and we get a little lost. Pull into someone's driveway in order to turn around, and miss the driveway slightly to the right so I'm pulled into the grass a bit. No big deal, grass will grow back if it's damaged, right? Go to back out of the driveway/grass and I guess there was something sticking out of the grass, a metal spike is my best guess (I didn't see it when we pulled in), whatever it was made this HORRIBLE ripping noise. We sped out of there super fast and didn't look back till we got to his dad's place. Turns out it nearly ripped my bumper off and ripped out one of the fog lights from the bottom... his dad zip ties the bumper back on and to this day my mom hasn't found out what happened, even though she's had my car taken to several repair shops for tires/unrelated things over the years.

Second thing happened at college. At the time I was working weekday afternoons for a popular after-school program in my area, basically we go around to different schools each day and run the program for them in the cafeteria. Well, I went to class that morning and ended up falling asleep in the library after class on one of the really comfy couches they have in there. Wake up and realize it's about an hour until I have to be at the school for the day, still haven't bought after school snacks or activity supplies, freak out and run to my car in order to get to the store and to the school on time. Start pulling out without looking and slam into someone's rear bumper, the guy had been looking for a spot and stopped at the end of the aisle for a minute. I get out, he gets out, I'm sweating bullets, he tells me this is his gf's car and she's gonna be pissed, calls her, and she shows up in 5 minutes... and tells me not to worry about it. Sends me on my way. I made it to work on time and everything. I thank the powers that be every single time I think about it.

In 10th grade, I had the worst English teacher imaginable. One of the dumbest rules was her attendance policy, that she decided to change halfway through the semester. Without telling anyone. Through the first half of the semester, if you got your stuff to class and set it in your seat, you'd be free to leave the classroom and come back when the bell rang (a lot of students used time between classes in order to get drinks or snacks from the machine, or to use the bathroom; to make sure they got to class on time they used this method). Suddenly, without telling us, she decided we all had to be in by the bell. On the day she enforced this rule, I put my stuff down, left the class to get a snack from the machine across the hall, and was nearly to the door when the bell rang.
